diagnosis: Immortal time bias in an observational survival analysis
mechanism: Immortal time bias occurs when a period during which participants must remain alive and outcome-free in order to later be classified as exposed is incorrectly assigned to the exposed group's follow-up, creating an artificial survival advantage.
vignette: Investigators use electronic health records to compare survival after a new cancer diagnosis. Patients are classified as 'treated' if they begin a study drug at any time during the first 90 days after diagnosis; all others are classified as untreated. Follow-up for both groups begins on the date of diagnosis. Patients who die before receiving the drug can only be placed in the untreated group.
lead: Which of the following biases most directly threatens the validity of the apparent survival benefit in the treated group?
distractor_notes: Lead-time bias arises when earlier detection appears to prolong survival without changing the time of death; this study's problem is exposure classification during follow-up.
Length-time bias arises because screening preferentially detects slower-growing disease; no screening-based case ascertainment is described.

Confounding by indication is possible in nonrandomized treatment studies but does not specifically describe the guaranteed survival interval between cohort entry and treatment assignment in this design.
Recall bias affects retrospective self-reported exposure or outcome information and is not the time-dependent classification error shown here.
key_expl: To enter the treated group, a patient must survive from diagnosis until the drug is started. If that pre-treatment interval is counted as treated follow-up, it is 'immortal' because death during that interval would prevent classification as treated. This systematically favors the treated group and is immortal time bias.
objective: Recognize immortal time bias when survival before a time-dependent exposure is incorrectly credited to the exposed group.
clues: treatment can begin after cohort entry
treated status assigned based on future exposure
patients must survive to receive treatment
